turnaround_reason: A high-quality OSA-implant maker whose stock fell from ~$147 to ~$39 on fears that GLP-1 drugs (Zepbound approved for OSA) will erode its addressable market; it is basing as management argues GLP-1s expand OSA diagnosis rather than replace implants.
bullish_points: Excellent unit economics: ~86% gross margin, profitable (~15% net margin), net cash (EV < market cap) — a real business, not a falling-knife shell.
Management survey of 200+ sleep physicians suggests GLP-1 availability is increasing the number of patients seeking OSA diagnosis/treatment, expanding the funnel.
+19% over 30 days off a deeply washed-out base; sentiment may be over-discounting the GLP-1 threat.
Rich options IV (~64%) lets holders sell premium or structure defined-risk upside.
bearish_points: GLP-1 competitive overhang is structural, not a one-quarter blip — an analyst flags the problem persisting into 2028.
Guidance was lowered; revenue growth is negative (-7.6% TTM) as patients delay implants to try weight-loss drugs first.
Not statistically cheap: fwd P/E ~41 for a decelerating grower.
Added noise from a Medicare fee change and new lawsuits.
catalyst: Evidence GLP-1s expand rather than cannibalize the OSA funnel; a guidance beat/reset that stabilizes the growth narrative.
suggested_trade: Small starter spot; better expressed selling premium given elevated IV, add on a stabilized growth print.
key_risk: GLP-1 adoption structurally shrinks Inspire's addressable market faster than management expects.
would_skip_if: You think GLP-1s permanently cap OSA-implant demand, or you won't pay ~40x for a decelerating grower.
